7:1.sourceText: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα περιεπάτει ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ· οὐ γὰρ ἤθελεν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περιπατεῖν, ὅτι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι.
7:1.targetText: And Jesus was walking after these things in Galilee, for He did not wish to walk in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill Him,

7:2.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἡ σκηνοπηγία.
7:2.targetText: and the celebration of the Jews was near—that of Shelters—

7:3.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Μετάβηθι ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν, ἵνα καὶ οἱ μαθηταί σου θεωρήσουσιν τὰ ἔργα σοῦ ἃ ποιεῖς·
7:3.targetText: His brothers, therefore, said to Him, “Depart from here, and go away to Judea, that Your disciples may also behold Your works that You do;

groups.note: N1904 θεωρήσουσιν is future indicative (they will behold), whereas LSV may behold corresponds to the subjunctive θεωρήσωσιν reading. The behold lexeme is shared without claiming identical mood/tense.

7:4.sourceText: οὐδεὶς γάρ τι ἐν κρυπτῷ ποιεῖ καὶ ζητεῖ αὐτὸς ἐν παρρησίᾳ εἶναι. εἰ ταῦτα ποιεῖς, φανέρωσον σεαυτὸν τῷ κόσμῳ.
7:4.targetText: for no one does anything in secret, and himself seeks to be in public; if you do these things—reveal Yourself to the world”;

7:5.sourceText: οὐδὲ γὰρ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπίστευον εἰς αὐτόν.
7:5.targetText: for not even His brothers were believing in Him.

7:6.sourceText: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς οὔπω πάρεστιν, ὁ δὲ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος πάντοτέ ἐστιν ἕτοιμος.
7:6.targetText: Jesus, therefore, says to them, “My time is not yet present, but your time is always ready;

7:7.sourceText: οὐ δύναται ὁ κόσμος μισεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἐμὲ δὲ μισεῖ, ὅτι ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστιν.
7:7.targetText: the world is not able to hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify concerning it that its works are evil.

7:8.sourceText: ὑμεῖς ἀνάβητε εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν· ἐγὼ οὔπω ἀναβαίνω εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην, ὅτι ὁ ἐμὸς καιρὸς οὔπω πεπλήρωται.
7:8.targetText: You—go up to this celebration; I do not yet go up to this celebration, because My time has not yet been fulfilled”;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV adds this to the first celebration phrase; pinned N1904 has only τὴν ἑορτήν there, without a demonstrative.

7:9.sourceText: ταῦτα δὲ εἰπὼν αὐτοῖς ἔμεινεν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ.
7:9.targetText: and saying these things to them, He remained in Galilee.

7:10.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἀνέβησαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν, τότε καὶ αὐτὸς ἀνέβη, οὐ φανερῶς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἐν κρυπτῷ.
7:10.targetText: And when His brothers went up, then also He Himself went up to the celebration, not openly, but as in secret;

7:11.sourceText: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ καὶ ἔλεγον Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος;
7:11.targetText: the Jews, therefore, were seeking Him in the celebration, and said, “Where is that One?”

7:12.sourceText: καὶ γογγυσμὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ ἦν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς ὄχλοις· οἱ μὲν ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἀγαθός ἐστιν, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον Οὔ, ἀλλὰ πλανᾷ τὸν ὄχλον.
7:12.targetText: And there was much murmuring about Him among the multitudes, some indeed said, “He is good”; and others said, “No, but He leads the multitude astray”;

unmappedSource.reason: Discourse construction: ὅτι introduces the quoted He is good claim; LSV uses direct speech with no separate that.

7:13.sourceText: οὐδεὶς μέντοι παρρησίᾳ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
7:13.targetText: no one, however, was speaking freely about Him, through fear of the Jews.

7:14.sourceText: Ἤδη δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκεν.
7:14.targetText: And it being now the middle of the celebration, Jesus went up to the temple, and He was teaching,

7:15.sourceText: ἐθαύμαζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες Πῶς οὗτος γράμματα οἶδεν μὴ μεμαθηκώς;
7:15.targetText: and the Jews were wondering, saying, “How has this One known letters—having not learned?”

groups.note: N1904 οὖν is continuative then/therefore; LSV uses and, matching the connective καί in the TR reading. The contextual transition is linked without claiming identical discourse force.

7:16.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν Ἡ ἐμὴ διδαχὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὴ ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με·
7:16.targetText: Jesus answered them and said, “My teaching is not Mine, but His who sent Me;

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness/wording difference: N1904 οὖν (then/therefore) has no separately expressed English connective in the LSV answer clause.

7:17.sourceText: ἐάν τις θέλῃ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν, γνώσεται περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς, πότερον ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ἢ ἐγὼ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ λαλῶ.
7:17.targetText: if anyone may will to do His will, he will know concerning the teaching, whether it is of God, or—[if] I speak from Myself.

unmappedTarget.reason: Translation addition: LSV supplies a second interrogative/conditional marker after or; N1904 has ἢ without an additional εἰ or ἐάν.

7:18.sourceText: ὁ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ· ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν, οὗτος ἀληθής ἐστιν καὶ ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν.
7:18.targetText: He who is speaking from himself seeks his own glory, but he who is seeking the glory of him who sent him, this one is true, and unrighteousness is not in him;

7:19.sourceText: οὐ Μωϋσῆς ἔδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν νόμον; καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ποιεῖ τὸν νόμον. τί με ζητεῖτε ἀποκτεῖναι;
7:19.targetText: has not Moses given you the Law? And none of you does the Law; why do you seek to kill Me?”

7:20.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ ὄχλος Δαιμόνιον ἔχεις· τίς σε ζητεῖ ἀποκτεῖναι;
7:20.targetText: The multitude answered and said, “You have a demon, who seeks to kill You?”

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV adds and said after answered; N1904 begins the direct reply without a corresponding καὶ εἶπεν clause.

7:21.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἓν ἔργον ἐποίησα καὶ πάντες θαυμάζετε.
7:21.targetText: Jesus answered and said to them, “I did one work, and you all wonder,

7:22.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὴν περιτομήν, —οὐχ ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐστὶν ἀλλ’ ἐκ τῶν πατέρων,— καὶ ἐν σαββάτῳ περιτέμνετε ἄνθρωπον.
7:22.targetText: because of this, Moses has given you the circumcision—not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers—and on a Sabbath you circumcise a man;

7:23.sourceText: εἰ περιτομὴν λαμβάνει ἄνθρωπος ἐν σαββάτῳ ἵνα μὴ λυθῇ ὁ νόμος Μωϋσέως, ἐμοὶ χολᾶτε ὅτι ὅλον ἄνθρωπον ὑγιῆ ἐποίησα ἐν σαββάτῳ;
7:23.targetText: if a man receives circumcision on a Sabbath that the Law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with Me that I made a man all whole on a Sabbath?

7:24.sourceText: μὴ κρίνετε κατ’ ὄψιν, ἀλλὰ τὴν δικαίαν κρίσιν κρίνατε.
7:24.targetText: Do not judge according to appearance, but the righteous judgment judge.”

7:25.sourceText: Ἔλεγον οὖν τινες ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμειτῶν Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὃν ζητοῦσιν ἀποκτεῖναι;
7:25.targetText: Certain, therefore, of the Jerusalemites said, “Is this not He whom they are seeking to kill?

7:26.sourceText: καὶ ἴδε παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖ καὶ οὐδὲν αὐτῷ λέγουσιν. Μή ποτε ἀληθῶς ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἄρχοντες ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός;
7:26.targetText: And behold, He speaks freely, and they say nothing to Him; did the rulers truly know that this is the Christ?

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή ποτε gives the question a tentative/negative-expectation force (can it be that?/surely not?); LSV asks did the rulers truly know without a separate corresponding particle expression.

7:27.sourceText: ἀλλὰ τοῦτον οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν· ὁ δὲ Χριστὸς ὅταν ἔρχηται, οὐδεὶς γινώσκει πόθεν ἐστίν.
7:27.targetText: But this One—we have known where He is from; and the Christ, when He comes, no one knows where He is from.”

7:28.sourceText: ἔκραξεν οὖν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λέγων Κἀμὲ οἴδατε καὶ οἴδατε πόθεν εἰμί· καὶ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλήλυθα, ἀλλ’ ἔστιν ἀληθινὸς ὁ πέμψας με, ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε·
7:28.targetText: Jesus cried, therefore, in the temple, teaching and saying, “You have both known Me, and you have known from where I am; and I have not come of Myself, but He who sent Me is true, whom you have not known;

7:29.sourceText: ἐγὼ οἶδα αὐτόν, ὅτι παρ’ αὐτοῦ εἰμι κἀκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν.
7:29.targetText: and I have known Him, because I am from Him, and He sent Me.”

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV begins and, corresponding to an extra δέ connective in its reading; pinned N1904 starts with ἐγώ (I) without a connective.

7:30.sourceText: Ἐζήτουν οὖν αὐτὸν πιάσαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπέβαλεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὴν χεῖρα, ὅτι οὔπω ἐληλύθει ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ.
7:30.targetText: They were seeking, therefore, to seize Him, and no one laid the hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come,

7:31.sourceText: Ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου δὲ πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἔλεγον Ὁ Χριστὸς ὅταν ἔλθῃ, μὴ πλείονα σημεῖα ποιήσει ὧν οὗτος ἐποίησεν;
7:31.targetText: and many out of the multitude believed in Him and said, “The Christ—when He may come—will He do more signs than these that this One did?”

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή marks a question expecting a negative answer; LSV asks will He do more without a separate negative particle.

7:32.sourceText: Ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τοῦ ὄχλου γογγύζοντος περὶ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὑπηρέτας ἵνα πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.
7:32.targetText: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning Him, and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers that they may take Him;

7:33.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἔτι χρόνον μικρὸν μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι καὶ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με.
7:33.targetText: Jesus, therefore, said to them, “Yet a short time I am with you, and I go away to Him who sent Me;

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV includes the recipient to them; pinned N1904 has no αὐτοῖς or corresponding recipient phrase in this verse.

7:34.sourceText: ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν.
7:34.targetText: you will seek Me, and you will not find; and where I am, you are not able to come.”

7:35.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς ἑαυτούς Ποῦ οὗτος μέλλει πορεύεσθαι, ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐχ εὑρήσομεν αὐτόν; μὴ εἰς τὴν Διασπορὰν τῶν Ἑλλήνων μέλλει πορεύεσθαι καὶ διδάσκειν τοὺς Ἕλληνας;
7:35.targetText: The Jews, therefore, said among themselves, “To where is this One about to go that we will not find Him? Is He about to go to the dispersion of the Greeks, and to teach the Greeks?

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή signals an expected negative answer in the Greek question; LSV Is He about to go has no separately expressed negative particle.

7:36.sourceText: τίς ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ὃν εἶπεν Ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν;
7:36.targetText: What is this word that He said, You will seek Me, and you will not find? And, Where I am, you are not able to come?”

7:37.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ μεγάλῃ τῆς ἑορτῆς εἱστήκει ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἔκραξεν λέγων Ἐάν τις διψᾷ, ἐρχέσθω πρός με καὶ πινέτω.
7:37.targetText: And in the last, the great day of the celebration, Jesus stood and cried, saying, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink;

7:38.sourceText: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμέ, καθὼς εἶπεν ἡ γραφή, ποταμοὶ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας αὐτοῦ ῥεύσουσιν ὕδατος ζῶντος.
7:38.targetText: he who is believing in Me, according as the Writing said, Rivers of living water will flow out of his belly”;

7:39.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν περὶ τοῦ Πνεύματος οὗ ἔμελλον λαμβάνειν οἱ πιστεύσαντες εἰς αὐτόν· οὔπω γὰρ ἦν Πνεῦμα, ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐδέπω ἐδοξάσθη.
7:39.targetText: and this He said of the Spirit, which those believing in Him were about to receive; for not yet was the Holy Spirit, because Jesus was not yet glorified.

groups.note: N1904 πιστεύσαντες is an aorist participle (those who believed); LSV believing corresponds to the present participial reading. The believe lexeme is shared without asserting identical aspect.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV qualifies the second Spirit reference as Holy; pinned N1904 has Πνεῦμα without an Ἅγιον qualifier here.

7:40.sourceText: Ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου οὖν ἀκούσαντες τῶν λόγων τούτων ἔλεγον Οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ προφήτης·
7:40.targetText: Many, therefore, out of the multitude, having heard the word, said, “This is truly the Prophet”;

groups.note: N1904 τῶν λόγων is plural (the words), while LSV has singular the word. This is a lexical correspondence across the different number reading, not identical inflection.

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness difference: N1904 has τούτων (these) qualifying words; LSV has the word without a corresponding demonstrative.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV explicitly says Many; pinned N1904 has no πολλοί quantifier in this verse.

7:41.sourceText: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός· οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον Μὴ γὰρ ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ὁ Χριστὸς ἔρχεται;
7:41.targetText: others said, “This is the Christ”; and others said, “Why, does the Christ come out of Galilee?

groups.note: The LSV interjection Why introduces the rhetorical question rendered from the Greek μή γάρ question formula. The formula is linked as a whole; neither γάρ alone nor μή alone is claimed to mean the lexical interrogative why.

7:42.sourceText: οὐχ ἡ γραφὴ εἶπεν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Δαυεὶδ, καὶ ἀπὸ Βηθλεὲμ τῆς κώμης ὅπου ἦν Δαυεὶδ, ἔρχεται ὁ Χριστός;
7:42.targetText: Did the Writing not say that out of the seed of David, and from Beth-Lehem—the village where David was—the Christ comes?”

7:43.sourceText: σχίσμα οὖν ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ δι’ αὐτόν·
7:43.targetText: A division, therefore, arose among the multitude because of Him.

7:44.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἤθελον ἐξ αὐτῶν πιάσαι αὐτόν, ἀλλ’ οὐδεὶς ἐπέβαλεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας.
7:44.targetText: And certain of them were willing to seize Him, but no one laid hands on Him;

7:45.sourceText: Ἦλθον οὖν οἱ ὑπηρέται πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ Φαρισαίους, καὶ εἶπον αὐτοῖς ἐκεῖνοι Διὰ τί οὐκ ἠγάγετε αὐτόν;
7:45.targetText: the officers came, therefore, to the chief priests and Pharisees, and they said to them, “Why did you not bring Him?”

7:46.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ὑπηρέται Οὐδέποτε ἐλάλησεν οὕτως ἄνθρωπος, ὡς οὗτος λαλεῖ ὁ ἄνθρωπος.
7:46.targetText: The officers answered, “Never so spoke man—as this Man.”

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness difference: N1904 explicitly repeats λαλεῖ (speaks) in as this Man speaks; this second verb is absent from the pinned TR reading and LSV, which end as this Man.

7:47.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν αὐτοῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι Μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς πεπλάνησθε;
7:47.targetText: The Pharisees, therefore, answered them, “Have you also been led astray?

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή marks negative expectation; LSV Have you also been led astray has no separate negative particle.

7:48.sourceText: μή τις ἐκ τῶν ἀρχόντων ἐπίστευσεν εἰς αὐτὸν ἢ ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων;
7:48.targetText: Did anyone out of the rulers believe in Him? Or out of the Pharisees?

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή expects a negative answer to the rulers-believing question; LSV Did anyone has no separate negative particle.

7:49.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ὁ ὄχλος οὗτος ὁ μὴ γινώσκων τὸν νόμον ἐπάρατοί εἰσιν.
7:49.targetText: But this multitude, that is not knowing the Law, is accursed.”

groups.note: Greek uses plural εἰσιν with the members of the collective crowd; LSV uses singular is with multitude. This is ordinary collective agreement variation, not a changed referent.

7:50.sourceText: λέγει Νικόδημος πρὸς αὐτούς, ὁ ἐλθὼν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρότερον, εἷς ὢν ἐξ αὐτῶν
7:50.targetText: Nicodemus says to them—he who came by night to Him—being one of them,

unmappedSource.reason: Source witness difference: N1904 πρότερον means previously/before; LSV by night follows the νυκτός reading, not this temporal adverb.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source witness difference: LSV specifies night, corresponding to νυκτός in the TR reading; pinned N1904 has πρότερον (previously) instead.

7:51.sourceText: Μὴ ὁ νόμος ἡμῶν κρίνει τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐὰν μὴ ἀκούσῃ πρῶτον παρ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ γνῷ τί ποιεῖ;
7:51.targetText: “Does our law judge the Man, if it may not hear from Him first, and know what He does?”

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: the initial μή marks negative expectation; LSV Does our law judge has no separately expressed negative particle. The later not in if it may not hear belongs to the second μή at token 8.

7:52.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Μὴ καὶ σὺ ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶ; ἐραύνησον καὶ ἴδε ὅτι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας προφήτης οὐκ ἐγείρεται.
7:52.targetText: They answered and said to him, “Are you also out of Galilee? Search and see that a prophet has not risen out of Galilee”; [[

groups.note: N1904 ἐγείρεται is present (arises/is raised), whereas LSV has not risen follows the perfect-tense reading. The rise lexeme is shared without asserting identical tense/aspect.

unmappedSource.reason: Question construction: μή expects a negative answer; LSV Are you also out of Galilee has no separately expressed negative particle.

7:53.sourceText: (Καὶ ἐπορεύθη ἕκαστος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
7:53.targetText: and each one went on to his house, but Jesus went on to the Mount of Olives.

review.note: LSV includes the Mount of Olives clause at the end of 7:53; its actual N1904 location is 8:1. Foreign source references preserve those raw Greek identities across the chapter boundary. A John8 review must mark the corresponding 8:1 words as rendered here, not duplicate them in LSV8:1.
